findings.title: Duplicate charges on slow networks (payment step)
findings.statement: Duplicate charges on slow networks: a second tap on Pay before any visual response produces a second charge for the same order.
reproduction: Throttle to Slow 3G (or ~400ms+ RTT), enter card in the iframe, tap Pay, tap again within ~3s before any visual response.
Also reproduces via browser Back and resubmit, and via mobile double-tap that fires before JS handlers attach.
findings.impact: The customer is charged twice for one order and has no way to tell — there's no confirmation artifact to compare against. They discover it on a bank statement days later.
findings.fix: Disabling the button and adding a spinner is the UI half. Zero duplicate charges requires a server-side idempotency key minted when the checkout session is created and passed on every charge attempt.
tags: violates: zero duplicate charges (hard acceptance criterion)
